# Setu — Implementation Reference for Cline + Sarvam-105B

> **How to use this document:** Place this file in your project root as `SETU_REFERENCE.md`. In Cline, start your first prompt with: "Read SETU_REFERENCE.md and generate the project structure for Phase 1." Cline (powered by Sarvam-105B) will use this document as the complete specification for building the entire system.

---

## 1. Project Overview

**Name:** Setu (Sanskrit for "bridge") — bridges raw accounting data to clean finalisation.

**What it is:** A pipeline-gated accounting agent for CA firms using TallyPrime. It sits as an orchestration layer above Tally, enforces quality gates between 5 workflow stages, and prevents incomplete data from reaching finalisation. Built entirely on Sarvam AI APIs.

**Core principle:** No data advances to the next stage until it passes a quality gate. The agent produces review packets at every gate. A human approves before anything posts to Tally.

**Tech stack:** FastAPI (Python 3.12) backend, React 18 + Tailwind frontend, PostgreSQL 16, Redis 7, Celery, Docker Compose, TallyPrime XML/ODBC integration, Sarvam-105B + Sarvam-30B APIs.

**Hosting:** Your own Linux server. No external cloud. All financial data stays on your server. Only text snippets for LLM reasoning are sent to Sarvam API.

---

## 2. Pain Points Being Solved

The firm's current workflow has 5 stages. Today, data flows through them without quality checks, so problems compound downstream.

| Stage | What happens today | Where it breaks |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Data Collection | Manual follow-ups for bank statements, loan/MF/PF statements, 26AS/AIS, GST details, invoices, ledger confirmations | Information arrives late or incomplete; no tracking of what's missing; repeated follow-ups |
| 2. Reconciliation | Manual comparison: Books vs GST portal, Books vs 26AS, Bank vs books, TDS deducted vs paid, vendor ledger vs payments, loan sheet, salary sheet | Largest time sink; invoice-number matching inconsistent; no systematic classification of Matched / Not in Books / Not in Portal / Amount Difference |
| 3. Corrective Entries | Identify and post adjustments for mismatches found in Stage 2 | Discovered late; overlaps with TB preparation and audit; corrective entries trigger TB re-extraction |
| 4. TB Finalisation | Extract Trial Balance, clean it up, resolve suspense/opening/prepaid/ROC/advance tax/directors' remuneration | TB extracted before books are clean; corrected repeatedly; discussions with client/auditor become lengthy |
| 5. Audit/Tax Finalisation | Financial statements, tax computation, audit query resolution | Accounting issues found during audit cascade back to TB and financial statements; rework loops |

**One-sentence summary of the biggest pain point:** "Incomplete or unreconciled accounting data reaches the finalisation stage, requiring repeated follow-ups, manual reconciliation and correction of the Trial Balance before it can be discussed with the client/auditor."

### Pain point to pipeline stage mapping

| Pain point | Pipeline stage | Root cause |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Books not clean before TB | Stages 3-4 | No pre-TB quality gate; uncleared items surface late |
| 2. GST reconciliation issues | Stage 2 | No systematic match engine; invoice-number normalisation missing |
| 3. TDS compliance hard to verify invoice-wise | Stage 2 | TDS ledger is aggregate; no chain tracker from invoice to challan to return |
| 4. Information comes late | Stage 1 | No automated intake tracking or follow-up system |
| 5. Audit queries and corrections overlap | Stages 4-5 | No change-impact tracking; audit findings cascade back without version control |
| 7. Large manual reconciliation volume | Stage 2 | 9+ reconciliation types done manually |

---

## 3. Original SOP (Tally-based accounts work)

This is the firm's existing manual workflow that Setu automates.

### Bank
- Bank statements (PDF/Excel) are fed into Tally using SUVIT (AI software that converts statements to vouchers).
- Setu adds: pre-processing validation, ledger mapping, closing balance reconciliation before posting.

### Sales and Purchases
- Invoice-wise Excel sheets or scanned bills from clients, fed into Tally via SUVIT.
- Setu adds: Sarvam Vision extraction for scans, GSTIN/HSN validation, rate mismatch flagging, forex conversion using RBI reference rate.

### GST
- Sales invoices → GSTR-1 (output tax).
- Purchase bills → GSTR-3B (input tax / ITC), reconciled with IMS/GSTR-2B from GST portal.
- Setu adds: automated 4-way reconciliation (Matched / Not in Books / Not in Portal / Amount Difference), ITC eligibility flagging, GSTR-3B draft preparation.

### TDS
- TDS deducted on payments to creditors, deposited by 7th, quarterly return filed.
- Setu adds: invoice-to-challan-to-return chain tracker, per-section rate application, 26AS reconciliation.

### Closing/Journal Entries
- Sale invoices (INR + forex), expenses, salary sheet (ESI/PF/OT), stock valuation, depreciation, receivables/payables closing.
- Setu adds: automated JV drafting with LLM rationale, pre-TB checklist gate.

### MIS Reports (Monthly)
- Balance Sheet & P&L (Schedule III format), variation reports, loan EMI reconciliation, cost-centre reconciliation.
- Setu adds: automated report generation from Tally ODBC data with LLM-drafted variance explanations.

### Annual Work
- Depreciation on fixed assets, interest on unsecured loans, 26AS vs TDS-receivable reconciliation.
- Setu adds: deterministic computation, automated 26AS matching.

---

## 4. Solution Architecture

### 4.1 Layered Architecture

```
Layer 1: Presentation (React + WhatsApp intake)
    ↓ HTTPS / WebSocket
Layer 2: Orchestration (Sarvam Work Agents: lead agent + 6 sub-agents)
    ↓ Sub-agent calls / MCP tools
Layer 3: Service (8 reconciliation engines + Tally XML/ODBC + portal parsers)
    ↓ HTTP / SQL / File I/O
Layer 4: Data (PostgreSQL + File Storage + TallyPrime + Sarvam API)
```

### 4.2 Agent Architecture (Sarvam Work Agents sub-agents)

| Sub-agent | Model | Role | MCP Tools |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lead Agent (Pipeline Controller) | 105B | Orchestrates all stages, enforces gates, compiles review packets | All |
| Sub-1: Intake Tracker | 30B | WhatsApp/email document intake, checklist tracking, follow-up reminders | WhatsApp, Gmail, file storage |
| Sub-2: GST Recon Engine | 105B | GSTR-2B vs Books matching, 4-way classification, ITC eligibility | Tally XML/ODBC, GST portal JSON |
| Sub-3: TDS Chain Tracker | 105B | Invoice → deduction → payment → challan → return chain verification | Tally ODBC, TRACES parser |
| Sub-4: Corrective Entry Drafter | 105B | Drafts JVs from reconciliation exceptions, writes LLM rationale | Tally XML (write) |
| Sub-5: Pre-TB Gate Checker | 30B | 12-item checklist, BLOCK/FLAG/PASS logic, gate report generation | Tally ODBC (read) |
| Sub-6: Audit Response Drafter | 105B | Change-impact tracking, TB versioning, audit query responses | Tally ODBC, Sarvam 105B |

### 4.3 The 5-Stage Pipeline with Gates

```
Stage 1: Data Collection
    → GATE 1: All critical documents received? (Block if missing)
Stage 2: Reconciliation (8 engines run in parallel)
    → GATE 2: All exceptions reviewed? (Block until resolved or waived)
Stage 3: Corrective Entries (JV drafting, human approval, post to Tally)
    → GATE 3: All corrections posted? (Block until posted or waived)
Stage 4: TB Finalisation (Pre-TB checklist, TB extraction)
    → GATE 4: All BLOCK items resolved? (Block TB extraction)
Stage 5: Audit/Tax (FS prep, tax computation, audit responses, change tracking)
```

Gate states: `PASS` (confirmed clean), `BLOCK` (must resolve), `FLAG` (proceed with note). Reviewer can override a BLOCK with a documented reason (logged in audit trail).

### 4.4 Reconciliation Engines (Stage 2)

Each engine follows the same pattern: ingest → normalise → match → classify exceptions → produce review packet.

| Engine | Source A | Source B | Match Logic | Output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GST 2B vs Books | GSTR-2B JSON (portal) | Tally purchase register (ODBC) | GSTIN + invoice no (fuzzy) + date + taxable value | 4-way: Matched / Not in Books / Not in Portal / Amount Diff + ITC eligibility |
| 26AS vs Books | 26AS text (IT portal) | Tally TDS-receivable ledger | TAN + quarter + TDS amount + section | Per-deductor match, mismatches with reasons |
| Bank vs Books | Bank statement (Excel) | Tally bank ledger (ODBC) | Amount + date + narration (LLM-assisted) | Unmatched credits/debits, closing balance check |
| TDS Chain Tracker | Purchase invoices + TDS entries | TDS challans + TDS return | Invoice → deduction → payment → challan → return | Per-invoice chain status, break detection |
| Vendor Ledger vs Payments | Tally vendor ledger | Tally payment vouchers | Invoice no + payment reference | Unmatched payments, outstanding balances |
| Opening Balances Check | Opening balance sheet | Current-year transactions | Ledger account + carry-forward check | Unresolved opening items, suspense clearance |
| Loan Sheet Recon | Loan amortisation sheet | Bank EMI credits | EMI amount + date + bank credit ref | EMI mismatches, principal/interest split |
| Salary Sheet Recon | Salary Excel | Tally salary JV + PF/ESI challans | Employee-wise + component-wise | PF/ESI computation check, posting accuracy |

### 4.5 GST Reconciliation Engine — Deep Dive (the critical engine)

This is the most important component. Steps:

1. **Ingest:** Fetch GSTR-2B JSON from file storage. Fetch Tally purchase register via ODBC `SELECT` query. Parse both into normalised invoice objects: `{gstin, invoice_no, date, taxable_value, tax_amount, cgst, sgst, igst}`

2. **Normalise:** Strip invoice number prefixes/suffixes. Handle leading zeros. Normalise date formats to ISO. Trim GSTINs. This resolves ~30% of false mismatches.

3. **Match (fuzzy):** For each portal invoice, find best match in books using: exact GSTIN + Levenshtein distance on invoice number (≤ 2 edits) + date within ±7 days + taxable value within ±1%. Assign confidence: High (exact), Medium (fuzzy), Low (no match).

4. **Classify:** Bucket each invoice:
   - `Matched` — all fields align
   - `Not in Books` — in portal, not in Tally
   - `Not in Portal` — in Tally, not in portal
   - `Amount Diff` — matched on GSTIN + invoice no but value differs
   - Flag ITC eligibility per 2B supplier compliance status

5. **Compute ITC:** Sum eligible ITC (matched + supplier compliant). Sum ineligible ITC (supplier non-filer). Produce GSTR-3B draft figures.

6. **Review Packet:** Generate structured output: exception list with evidence per row, summary metrics, LLM-drafted plain-English explanation, drafted JVs for "Not in Books" items. Return to lead agent for gate check.

### 4.6 TDS Chain Tracker — Deep Dive

For each purchase invoice where TDS is applicable, track the full chain:

| Chain step | Data source | What to check |
|---|---|---|
| 1. TDS applicable? | Invoice nature + vendor status + section | Whether TDS should be deducted and at what rate |
| 2. TDS deducted? | Tally TDS deduction entry | Whether the deduction was booked against this invoice |
| 3. Vendor payment made? | Tally payment voucher | Whether vendor was paid (net of TDS) |
| 4. TDS paid to government? | TDS challan (CPI) | Whether deducted TDS was deposited via challan in correct period |
| 5. TDS in return? | TDS return (TRACES) | Whether challan appears in quarterly return against correct PAN/section |

Any break in the chain is flagged as an exception.

### 4.7 Pre-TB Quality Gate — 12 Items

| Check item | What to scan for | Gate status |
|---|---|---|
| Opening balances | All opening items cleared / carried forward | Block if unconfirmed |
| Suspense account | Zero balance or items identified | Block if unidentified balance |
| Excess receipts | Each identified and reclassified | Block if unexplained |
| Prepaid expenses | Prepaid portion amortised, balance justified | Flag if unusual |
| ROC payable | Confirmed against MDS portal | Block if unconfirmed |
| Advance tax | Reconciled with 26AS, instalments match | Block if mismatch |
| Directors' remuneration | Reconciled with DIR-12 / board resolution | Flag if total doesn't match |
| Bank balances | All bank ledgers reconciled, closing matches | Block if unreconciled |
| GST position | GSTR-3B filed, output tax and ITC reconciled | Block if open exceptions |
| TDS position | TDS return filed, ledger reconciled with challans/26AS | Block if open exceptions |
| Stock valuation | Stock register valued, closing confirmed | Flag if method changed |
| Depreciation | Posted as per Companies Act rates | Block if not posted |

## 5. Data Model (PostgreSQL Schema)

### 5.1 Core Tables

```sql
-- Client master
CREATE TABLE clients (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    tally_company_path VARCHAR(500),
    gstin VARCHAR(15),
    pan VARCHAR(10),
    financial_year VARCHAR(9),
    active BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- Per-client per-period pipeline state
CREATE TABLE pipeline_state (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    client_id INTEGER REFERENCES clients(id),
    period VARCHAR(7) NOT NULL,  -- YYYY-MM
    current_stage INTEGER DEFAULT 1,  -- 1-5
    status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'in_progress',  -- in_progress, blocked, done
    blocked_reason TEXT,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),
    UNIQUE(client_id, period)
);

-- Document checklist
CREATE TABLE document_checklist (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    client_id INTEGER REFERENCES clients(id),
    period VARCHAR(7),
    doc_type VARCHAR(50),  -- bank, gstr2b, 26as, bills, salary, loan, pf
    expected_date DATE,
    received_date TIMESTAMP,
    received_via VARCHAR(20),  -- whatsapp, email, upload
    file_path VARCHAR(500),
    status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'pending'  -- pending, received
);

-- Follow-up reminder history
CREATE TABLE followup_history (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    client_id INTEGER REFERENCES clients(id),
    doc_type VARCHAR(50),
    reminder_no INTEGER,  -- 1, 2, 3
    sent_via VARCHAR(20),
    sent_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),
    status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'sent'  -- sent, escalated, acknowledged
);

-- Reconciliation exceptions
CREATE TABLE reconciliation_exceptions (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    client_id INTEGER REFERENCES clients(id),
    period VARCHAR(7),
    engine_type VARCHAR(30),  -- gst_2b, 26as, bank, tds_chain, vendor, opening, loan, salary
    source_a_ref VARCHAR(200),  -- invoice no / challan no / etc
    source_b_ref VARCHAR(200),
    exception_type VARCHAR(30),  -- not_in_books, not_in_portal, amount_diff, chain_break
    details JSONB,  -- full exception context
    confidence VARCHAR(10),  -- high, medium, low
    status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'pending',  -- pending, approved, rejected, waived
    reviewed_by VARCHAR(100),
    reviewed_at TIMESTAMP
);

-- Drafted journal vouchers
CREATE TABLE drafted_jvs (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    exception_id INTEGER REFERENCES reconciliation_exceptions(id),
    client_id INTEGER REFERENCES clients(id),
    voucher_date DATE,
    narration TEXT,
    lines JSONB,  -- [{account, dr, cr}, ...]
    status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'drafted',  -- drafted, approved, posted, rejected
    posted_voucher_no VARCHAR(50),  -- Tally voucher number after posting
    approved_by VARCHAR(100),
    approved_at TIMESTAMP
);

-- Pre-TB gate reports
CREATE TABLE gate_reports (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    client_id INTEGER REFERENCES clients(id),
    period VARCHAR(7),
    items JSONB,  -- [{name, state, detail}, ...]
    overrides JSONB,  -- [{item, reason, by, at}, ...]
    overall_status VARCHAR(20),  -- passed, blocked
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- Trial Balance version history
CREATE TABLE tb_versions (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    client_id INTEGER REFERENCES clients(id),
    period VARCHAR(7),
    version_no INTEGER,
    tb_data JSONB,  -- full trial balance
    delta_from_prior JSONB,  -- what changed
    trigger_reason VARCHAR(50),  -- initial, audit_correction, manual
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- Immutable audit trail
CREATE TABLE audit_trail (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    client_id INTEGER REFERENCES clients(id),
    action VARCHAR(30),  -- approve, reject, override, post, reverse
    entity_type VARCHAR(30),  -- exception, jv, gate_item, tb
    entity_id INTEGER,
    user_id VARCHAR(100),
    timestamp TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),
    reason TEXT,
    metadata JSONB
);

-- Generated review packets
CREATE TABLE review_packets (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    client_id INTEGER REFERENCES clients(id),
    period VARCHAR(7),
    stage INTEGER,
    packet_type VARCHAR(30),  -- recon, gate, corrective, audit
    content JSONB,
    ai_summary TEXT,
    confidence VARCHAR(10),
    status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'pending',  -- pending, reviewed
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- Per-client configuration (JSONB for flexibility)
CREATE TABLE client_config (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    client_id INTEGER REFERENCES clients(id),
    ledger_mappings JSONB,  -- {tally_ledger: gst_rate, hsn, tds_section}
    gst_rate_master JSONB,
    tds_sections JSONB,
    gate_checklist_config JSONB,
    schedule_iii_template JSONB
);

## 9. Tally Integration

### 9.1 ODBC Read (for reports, ledgers, trial balance)

```python
# src/tally/odbc_reader.py
import pyodbc

def get_tally_connection(dsn: str = "TallyODBC_9000"):
    return pyodbc.connect(f"DSN={dsn}")

def fetch_purchase_register(client_period: str):
    """Fetch purchase register from Tally via ODBC."""
    conn = get_tally_connection()
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    cursor.execute("""
        SELECT $Name, $Date, $PartyName, $VoucherNumber, 
               $Amount, $GSTIN, $TaxableValue, $TaxAmount
        FROM Vouchers 
        WHERE $VoucherType = 'Purchase'
        AND $Date BETWEEN ? AND ?
    """)
    rows = cursor.fetchall()
    conn.close()
    return rows

def fetch_trial_balance():
    """Fetch trial balance from Tally via ODBC."""
    conn = get_tally_connection()
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    cursor.execute("""
        SELECT $Name, $ClosingBalance 
        FROM Ledger 
        ORDER BY $Name
    """)
    rows = cursor.fetchall()
    conn.close()
    return rows
```

### 9.2 XML Write (for posting vouchers)

```python
# src/tally/xml_writer.py
import httpx

TALLY_URL = "http://localhost:9000"

async def post_voucher_to_tally(voucher_xml: str) -> dict:
    """Post a voucher to Tally via XML-over-HTTP."""
    async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client:
        response = await client.post(
            TALLY_URL,
            content=voucher_xml,
            headers={"Content-Type": "text/xml"},
            timeout=30.0
        )
        # Parse Tally response for CRE (Created) confirmation
        return {"success": "CRE" in response.text, "response": response.text}

def build_purchase_voucher(
    date: str,
    party: str,
    taxable_value: float,
    cgst: float,
    sgst: float,
    narration: str
) -> str:
    """Build Tally XML for a purchase voucher."""
    return f"""
    <ENVELOPE>
        <HEADER>
            <TALLYREQUEST>Import Data</TALLYREQUEST>
        </HEADER>
        <BODY>
            <IMPORTDATA>
                <REQUESTDESC>
                    <REPORTNAME>Vouchers</REPORTNAME>
                </REQUESTDESC>
                <DATA>
                    <TALLYMESSAGE>
                        <VOUCHER VCHTYPE="Purchase" ACTION="Create">
                            <DATE>{date}</DATE>
                            <PARTYNAME>{party}</PARTYNAME>
                            <NARRATION>{narration}</NARRATION>
                            <ALLLEDGERENTRIES.LIST>
                                <LEDGERNAME>Purchase A/c</LEDGERNAME>
                                <ISDEEMEDPOSITIVE>No</ISDEEMEDPOSITIVE>
                                <AMOUNT>{taxable_value}</AMOUNT>
                            </ALLLEDGERENTRIES.LIST>

The document proposes a Lead Agent + 6 sub-agents. I recommend a refined structure that adds **verification and confidence-gating**, because with a single LLM model, accuracy lives in the orchestration, not the model tier.

### Three tiers of agents (not two)

```
Tier A — Deterministic Engines (NO LLM)          ← Highest accuracy, zero hallucination
Tier B — LLM Reasoning Agents (sarvam-105b)      ← Judgement, classification, drafting
Tier C — Verification Agents (sarvam-105b)       ← Second-opinion / consistency checks
```

**Core accuracy principle:** Anything that can be expressed as a rule (date math, amount comparison, GSTIN validation, HSN lookup, TDS rate application, balance zero-checks, Levenshtein matching, ITC eligibility rules from 2B flags) runs in **Tier A deterministic Python code**. The LLM never does arithmetic or strict rule application. The LLM only does: ambiguous classification, narration/rationale drafting, and natural-language summarization — and every LLM output that has a deterministic anchor is re-verified against Tier A.

| 2 | **Document Extractor** (NEW) | Sarvam Vision + 105B | A+B | PDF/image → structured data via Vision, then LLM normalization | Vision output validated against expected schema; LLM only normalizes/cleans |
| 3 | **GST Recon Engine** | 105B | A+B | 2B vs Books 4-way match, ITC eligibility | Fuzzy matching = Tier A (Levenshtein); LLM only resolves borderline matches with confidence + evidence |

### The two accuracy-critical patterns to build in

**Pattern 1 — Drafter/Verifier split (for Sub-6 and Sub-8):**
For any LLM output that produces an artifact with correctness constraints (a JV, a tax computation, an audit response), make **two independent sarvam-105b calls** with different prompts and different temperature:
- **Drafter** (temperature 0.2): produces the JV with narration.
- **Verifier** (temperature 0.0, different system prompt): receives the draft + the exception context + a checklist ("are debits=credits? is the ledger a valid Tally ledger? does the narration match the exception?") and returns PASS/FAIL with reasons.
- Only if Verifier passes does the JV become `drafted` status. This catches ~the majority of LLM drafting errors at the cost of one extra API call.

**Pattern 2 — Confidence-gated escalation (for Sub-3 and Sub-5):**
Every LLM classification returns a `confidence` (high/medium/low). Low-confidence items never auto-resolve; they are flagged for human review with the LLM's reasoning shown as *advice*, not as a decision. This is the "BLOCK if confidence < threshold" rule that protects accuracy under your single-model constraint.

### New sub-agent to add: Document Extractor (Sub-2 in my list)

The original document folds document extraction into "intake," but for accuracy you want it isolated because **Sarvam Vision output is structured data that must be validated before it enters any reconciliation.** This agent:
1. Calls Sarvam Vision (`/doc-digitization/job/v1`) on uploaded PDFs/scans.
2. Parses the markdown/JSON output into normalized invoice/bank/26AS objects.
3. Runs schema validation (required fields, types, GSTIN checksum, HSN format).
4. Flags extraction confidence; low-confidence extractions go to manual review, NOT to recon.

This is where most accounting data-entry errors originate, so isolating it with its own validation is the single biggest accuracy lever.

## Part 3 — Accuracy-Focused Design Decisions (your top priority)

Given you only have sarvam-105b, these are the decisions that determine whether your product is trustworthy:

1. **Never let the LLM do arithmetic.** All sums, differences, rate applications, date math = Python. The LLM sees pre-computed numbers and only classifies/ narrates.

2. **Structured outputs everywhere.** Use strict JSON schemas for every LLM call and validate with Pydantic. A malformed LLM response = exception, not a silent wrong value. Reject and retry on schema failure (max 2 retries).

3. **Drafter/Verifier on every write-path LLM call** (JVs, audit responses, gate overrides drafted by AI). Cost: +1 API call. Benefit: catches the highest-severity errors.

4. **Confidence gating + human-in-the-loop.** Low-confidence classifications route to human review with AI advice shown, never auto-applied. The pipeline's gates (Section 4.3) are your accuracy contract: nothing posts without human approval.

# Setu AI Build Team

A team of 8 AI subagent roles that *build* the Setu accounting pipeline. These are
**build-time agents** (they construct the product), distinct from Setu's **runtime
agents** (the Lead + 6 sub-agents that operate the finished pipeline).

All agents run on **Sarvam-105B** (the sole current Sarvam chat model; sarvam-30b is
deprecated). The broader Sarvam API family (Vision, Translation, etc.) is baked *into*
the Setu product itself — see `Setu_Implementation_Reference.md` Section 8.

## Accuracy philosophy (read first)

Setu is a financial-accuracy product. The team's process mirrors the product's process:

1. **Deterministic Tier-A code first.** Anything rule-based (date math, amount
   comparison, GSTIN/HSN validation, TDS rates, balance checks, Levenshtein matching,
   ITC eligibility) is written as pure Python/SQL — **the LLM never does arithmetic.**
2. **Review-gated, not free-flowing.** Specialists don't merge work directly. The
   Team Lead collects, reviews, integrates, and signs off — the build-time analogue
   of Setu's pipeline gates.
3. **Drafter/Verifier on LLM-output code.** When an engineer writes a function that
   *invokes* sarvam-105b at runtime (e.g. JV drafting), QA runs a second independent
   review pass on the prompt + output schema.
4. **Human-in-the-loop at every gate.** Full autonomy is the wrong goal for a
   financial product. The human (you / the CA) approves at each phase gate.

## The roster

| # | Role file | Sarvam model | Owns |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `orchestrator.md` | 105b | Team Lead — dispatch, review gates, sign-off |
| 2 | `product-manager.md` | 105b | Phase requirements + acceptance criteria |
| 3 | `backend-engineer.md` | 105b | FastAPI, engines, Tally, Sarvam clients, Celery |
| 4 | `frontend-engineer.md` | 105b | React + Tailwind, 4 screens, evidence UI |
| 5 | `domain-accounting.md` ⭐ | 105b | GST/TDS/ITC/TB/depreciation rules (accuracy lynchpin) |
| 6 | `security-compliance.md` | 105b | DPDP, audit trail, RBAC, data residency |
| 7 | `testing-qa.md` | 105b | Golden test sets, accuracy regression, Drafter/Verifier |
| 8 | `devops.md` | 105b | Docker, Alembic, env, CI, reproducible builds |

⭐ Domain-Accounting is where accuracy is won or lost — every deterministic rule must
be encoded correctly and validated against the SOP (reference doc Section 3).

## How to use this team (Option A — manual role-switching)

1. Start a Cline session in the `setu/` folder.
2. **Load a role:** tell Cline *"Operate as the role defined in `.agents/<role>.md` for
   the following task: ..."*. Cline reads the file and adopts that persona, scope, and
   constraints for the task.
3. **Hand-off:** each role's output lands as a file in the workspace (e.g. PM writes
   `requirements/phase-0-req.md`). The next role reads that artifact as input.
4. **Switch roles** for the next task. One role per task per session keeps scope clean.
5. **Review gates:** before a phase advances, the Team Lead runs the
   `templates/review-gate-checklist.md` and a human approves.

```
PM ──► requirements/phase-N-req.md

Team Lead ──► requirements/phase-N-tasks.md  (decomposition)
         │
Backend / Frontend / Domain ──► src/** , frontend/**  (parallel where independent)
         │
Security ──► reviews anything touching data/auth/Tally/external

QA ──► tests/** + golden sets + accuracy-regression-report
         │
Team Lead ──► review-gate-checklist + sign-off
         │
Human ──► approve ──► next phase
```

- `templates/task-breakdown.md` — Team Lead dispatch format
- `templates/review-gate-checklist.md` — per-role gate criteria
- `templates/accuracy-regression-report.md` — QA regression output format

These roles build Setu. They do **not** implement Setu's runtime Lead/sub-agents (that
is product code the Backend/Domain engineers write *during* the phases). Keep the two
layers separate to avoid confusion.

# Role: Team Lead / Tech Lead (Orchestrator)

You are the **Team Lead** for building Setu, a pipeline-gated accounting agent for CA
firms. You orchestrate the other 7 build-team roles, own architecture, enforce review
gates, and hold final sign-off authority before a phase advances.

## Persona

You are a pragmatic senior tech lead with 10+ years in fintech/accounting systems. You

You are a chartered-accountant-turned-engineer. You know the Companies Act, GST Act,
and TDS provisions cold, and you know exactly which rules are deterministic vs which
need human judgement. You never approximate a tax rule — if a rate depends on a
condition, you encode the condition, not a guess. You validate every rule against the

## Scope (you do this)

- GST rate master + HSN validation + GSTIN checksum validation (Section 3 Sales/Purchases).

- Document a `docs/rule-source.md` mapping each encoded rule to its legal/SOP source.

## The cardinal rule (accuracy)

**Every rule you encode is deterministic and sourced.** No "the LLM will figure it
out." If a rule has an edge case (e.g. reverse charge, composition dealer, sectional
TDS threshold), you encode the edge case explicitly. You annotate each rule with its

read_files, search_codebase, editor, run_commands (run rule unit tests). Sarvam MCP

every integration boundary (Tally, WhatsApp, Sarvam, web).
